adjudicated.jp: 霧が赤面した。
adjudicated.en: Kiri went red in the face.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「つぎはなんだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What is even next now."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese asks roughly 'What next?' The English stacks incompatible focus adverbs into an ungrammatical question form.

adjudicated.jp: 「決まっています」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "That is obvious."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしは下を脱ぎなさいと言いました」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "I have said to remove your belows."
comments: See CCC0026 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Miki says she told him to take off his lower clothing. The English lacks the object of 'said to' and invents the plural noun 'belows.'

highlights.text: I have said to remove your belows.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: 「いいのか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You sure?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: シリアスに告げる。
adjudicated.en: So I proclaim with seriousness.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says only that he tells her seriously. The English adds a connective and inflates speech into proclamation.

adjudicated.jp: 「これを露出するということの意味、知ってのことか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That means to expose 'this' to the public, do you know that?"
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi asks whether she understands what exposing it means. The English adds 'to the public' and converts the embedded object into an ungrammatical assertion followed by a tag.

highlights.text: That means to expose 'this' to the public, do you know that?

adjudicated.jp: 「この期に及んでおどしですか？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Making threats at this late stage, are you?"
comments: Watch Miki take Taichi's crap even more seriously than HE does. If there were a metachuuni Settei working throughout, this is evidence she'd not only follow it, but be perfectly incapable of telling whether others are serious or not. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「馬鹿な。君はこいつの恐ろしさをわかっちゃいない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Fool! You fail to comprehend how scary this thing is!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「これはそのクロスボウのように、初心者にも容易く制御できる可愛らしいものじゃないんだぞ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You think it's like that crossbow, some sweet little thing that even a beginner can easily control?"
comments: That's, of course, kinda laughable. Sure, it's easier than a bow, but it's not that trivial. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「世界中の膜という膜、処女という処女を無限に貪り食う……まさに魔物」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "All throughout the world, endlessly will it greedily devour those membranes we call hymens, those girls we call virgins... it is truly a demon."
comments: The implication remains that Taichi's Monster is and has always been his sex drive. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ひとたび解放すれば、世界から処女の輝きが消えることは確実」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "If it is released but once, the disappearance of the dazzling radiance of virgin girls from the world is a certainty."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……世迷い言を」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "...meaningless whining."
adjudicated.assessment: 世迷い言 means nonsense or absurd talk. It does not characterize the speech as complaint or whining.

adjudicated.jp: 「ねぇ……わたしも別に見たくない……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Say... I don't really want to see it either..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「霧ちんは黙ってて」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Kiri-chin will be silent."
adjudicated.assessment: Miki directly tells Kiri to be quiet. The English changes the imperative into a third-person future prediction and carries over the altered honorific as an unexplained form.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...oh, 'K."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese is a hesitant assent. The clipped English slang spelling is unsupported.

adjudicated.jp: しょんぼり。
adjudicated.en: She's downhearted.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 美希は本気だ。
adjudicated.en: Miki is serious.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……すべてを無に帰すつもりか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...do you intend to return everything to nothing?"
comments: See CCB0022 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そうだと言ったら？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "What if I say I do?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なっ、君は、君というヤツは……それでも科学者か！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But! You... the person you are... you are still a scientist!"
comments: Doesn't seem so much a reference, as much as a masquerading of the simpler truth: Miki plays the "villain" by pushing her Dragon, Kiri, on Taichi because stories demand villains and their sidekicks. So Kiri is made to look like the villain, but she's just a manipulated puppet, and the true villain was the protagonist's pupil who turned to evil. This is all metagame within metagame. And then the true villain was coincidence, and coincidence was no villain but God. The End - Cross Channel. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: それでも科学者か challenges whether she can still call herself a scientist. The English instead affirms that she remains one.

adjudicated.jp: 「科学とは突き詰めるもの。科学とは禁忌の先を進み往くもの」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Science is thorough investigation to its inevitable conclusion. Science is the progress through and beyond the taboos."
comments: No it isn't, and no it isn't. Miki's a mad scientist, though, certainly. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「話全然みえない……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I can't see what you're talking about at all..."
comments: "Seeing" is important, of course. See Shimura Phenomenon: when Miki can't see... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「背後を見ながらの科学に、意味はないんですよ、教授」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Science performed while looking backwards is meaningless, Professor."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「くっ、悪魔に魂を売ったか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ngh, did you sell your soul to the devil?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そう、アインシュタインのようにです」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Indeed, just like Einstein."
comments: Robert Johnson. ...I actually thought that up as a stupid joke, but see CCA0008: this is the simplest explanation for why Taichi would call Miki with the name 'Johnson'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「やむをえん……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Can't avoid this..."
adjudicated.assessment: やむをえん means that the situation cannot be helped. The English leaves 'avoid' without an object and does not express reluctant acceptance.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は乳首に触れた。
adjudicated.en: I touched a nipple.
comments: The second will come into play later. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「この爆破スイッチを使うことになろうとは」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Then I will use this Self-Destruct Button!"
comments: See CCA0008, same term as his sexual molestation technique. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says he never thought he would have to use the detonation switch. The English omits that surprise and necessity, changes the statement to a future decision, and invents capitalization.

highlights.text: Then I will use this Self-Destruct Button!

adjudicated.assessment: The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: 霧はクロスボウをおいて、トイレに入った。
adjudicated.en: Kiri put away the crossbow and went into the toilet.
comments: Since it fits into her pocket anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese means that Kiri entered the restroom. In US English, going 'into the toilet' ordinarily means entering the fixture itself.

adjudicated.jp: 「爆破スイッチ？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Self-Destruct Button?"
comments: Wonder if she thinks he's about to assault her. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そうだ。私はこいつを、この悪魔の逸物を世に解きはなつわけにはいかんのだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Indeed. For I absolutely cannot let this... this mephistophelic masterpiece loose onto the world!"
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese hyperbolically calls it the devilish exceptional object. The English invents a rare adjective tied to Mephistopheles and upgrades the object to a masterpiece.

adjudicated.en: Miki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「すべての淑女に安らぎあれ。妻よ子よ、すまん……愚かな父を許せ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Be all at peace, ladies. My wife, my son, sorry... forgive your stupid father!"
comments: They're probably still lost somewhere on the mountains he stupidly mistook for a hill. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 子 does not specify the child's sex. The English invents a son.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...hm?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうしたことだ、これは？　装置が作動せんとは？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What is the meaning of this? Why doesn't the Device work?"
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese uses the common noun 'device.' Capitalizing it as a proper or branded name is unsupported.

adjudicated.jp: 「……ふふ、あなたの行動など、とうにお見通しだったのですよ、陛下！」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "...heheh, I have seen through all your actions and behaviors long ago, Your Highness!"
adjudicated.assessment: 陛下 is the address 'Your Majesty.' 'Your Highness' corresponds to a different rank and form of address.

adjudicated.jp: 「配役変わってるし……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "The cast has changed..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: トイレから戻った霧が、のろのろとクロスボウを構え直した。
adjudicated.en: Returning from the toilet, Kiri sluggishly readjusted her crossbow posture.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that Kiri sluggishly raises or takes aim with the crossbow again. The English makes the crossbow possess a posture that she readjusts.

adjudicated.jp: 「配線を……くそう！　なんてこった！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The wiring... dammit! The hell is this!"
comments: Wiring's not his specialty after all, see CCA0006. See CCB0022 again. Combine with Tower of Friends and... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「絶体絶命ですね」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "It is inescapable doom."
comments: On random and very much likely unrelated news, the Zettai Zetsumei Toshi series is 2002 at least... damn I really thought it was older. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 絶体絶命 identifies an inescapable predicament. The English supplies an empty pronoun and equates the situation with doom as a substance.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Heh..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「忘れたか、乳首は二つあるということを！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Did you forget now, that there are TWO nipples!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Miki: "?!?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「科学に溺れ、人間工学を怠った……美希君、キミの負けだ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wallowing in your science, ergonomics caught you off-guard... Miki-kun, this is how you are beat!"
comments: The subtext should be making your head spin right about here, especially considering she just goes and tries to kill him over this very comment. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says Miki became lost in science and neglected ergonomics, so she has lost. The English makes ergonomics catch her off guard and ends with the ungrammatical passive 'how you are beat.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Wallowing in your science, ergonomics caught you off-guard... Miki-kun, this is how you are beat!"

adjudicated.jp: 「させるか！」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "'Cause I'll let ya!"
comments: PCP CCC0006A
Hmmm. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: させるか means 'Like hell I'll let you!' The English says the exact opposite—that she will allow it—and adds an unsupported causal fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 美希は霧に飛びつく。

adjudicated.assessment: 切っ先 is the physical tip or point of the weapon. 'Point of attack' is a tactical abstraction.

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese calls the move the pinnacle or ultimate form of skirt-flipping. 'Extreme of' is not a grammatical English superlative construction.

adjudicated.jp: 「スカートへアクセスする、指先が布をつまむその一瞬、全身の関節２４箇所を同時駆動させることによって、女子下半身における魅惑的閉鎖空間内に極小の乱気流を発生させる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "On access to the skirt, that 1 instant in which the fingertips clench the cloth, I make 24 joints simultaneously operate so that inside the ravishing sealed space of the lower portions of a girl's body outbreaks a turbulence most minute."
comments: Sealed space = recurring term. Not certain what is meant with that joints things, there's 28 joints total on the hand, so which 4 are missing? 2+4=6,+1 (the 1 instant the operation takes) =7. Forced... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the fingertips pinch the fabric and the coordinated movement generates a tiny turbulence. 'Clench' does not take cloth this way, while the English makes the turbulence itself 'outbreak' in an inverted, ungrammatical clause.

adjudicated.jp: 「この作用により、めくりあげたスカートはパラシュート状に維持され、通常のスカートめくりの数倍の滞空時間をもって下着を衆目にさらしあげるのである！」

adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the lifted skirt is kept in a parachute shape. The English uses the wrong preposition and an unnecessarily literal state construction.

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧はばたばたとスカートを押さえつけている。
adjudicated.en: In a flap Kiri flaps her skirt down,
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri frantically holds or presses the skirt down. The English instead makes her flap it, conflating the idiom ばたばた with the physical motion of fabric.

adjudicated.jp: が、押さえれば反対側が、より高くふわりとめくりあがる。
adjudicated.en: but the side opposite of her flapping flips fluffily higher.
comments: I have avoided "flips fluffily further up". Be glad. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that whenever she presses one side down, the opposite side floats even higher. The English invents a side opposite to an action called flapping and fails to bind the two sides.

highlights.text: the side opposite of her flapping

adjudicated.jp: さりとて放置してもスカートはクラゲ状に、下着を露出し続ける。
adjudicated.en: But even if she were to leave it be, the medusiform skirt would continue to expose her underwear.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: まるで下方から風が吹き上げているかのように。
adjudicated.en: Exactly as if from the lower parts a wind were blowing upwards.
adjudicated.assessment: 下方 means 'from below.' 'The lower parts' can refer to a person's lower body and creates an unintended anatomical reading.

adjudicated.jp: 「反間の計。今まで味方だったものが、これからも味方であるとは限らない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Have counterintelligence measures. There is no certainty that those who have been allies thus far will be allies hereafter."
comments: Even though he's telling Kiri not to trust Miki, it doesn't really fit. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 反間の計 names a stratagem of turning an opponent's ally against them. The English changes this into an imperative to possess plural counterintelligence measures.

adjudicated.jp: 「この教訓をいかせよ、霧ちん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Make good use of this lesson, Kiri-chin!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「す、すかぁとがっ……ふわふわ浮いてっ、ちょっと、なにコレ！？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Sk-, the skiiirt... floating all fluffy! Really, what is this?!"
comments: It's FUCKING FUWA FUWA TIME it's what it is. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「スゴワザですねー……」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Amazing trick isn't it..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「可憐だ。霧ちん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Lovely, innit, Kiri-chin."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese simply calls her lovely. The specifically British tag is not present.

adjudicated.jp: 親指を立てた。
adjudicated.en: I stick my thumb up.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あぁあぁあぁぁぁあぁぁぁぁ……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "AaAaAaaaAaaaah..."
comments: 7x2 As total -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧ちんはあたふたしていた。
adjudicated.en: Kiri-chin was in a feverish haste.
adjudicated.assessment: あたふた means that she is flustered and panicking. 'Feverish haste' describes speed or urgency rather than her confusion.

adjudicated.jp: もし公衆の面前でやったら悶死するやもしれぬ。
adjudicated.en: If there was real public presence, she could mayhap even experience death in agony.
adjudicated.assessment: The English stacks two modal expressions, 'could' and 'mayhap,' in one clause and nominalizes dying as experiencing death.

adjudicated.jp: さすが奥義。
adjudicated.en: So is expected from Esoterica.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says, 'Just what you'd expect from a secret ultimate technique.' The English is missing a subject and uses 'esoterica,' a plural or mass noun for obscure knowledge, as the name of the move.

adjudicated.jp: 曜子ちゃんとか全然動じないからなぁ。
adjudicated.en: Youko-chan for example wouldn't be moved at all wouldn't she.
adjudicated.assessment: The English attaches an affirmative tag to a negative predicate and omits the punctuation that would separate it.

highlights.text: wouldn't be moved at all wouldn't she

adjudicated.jp: やっぱ慌てふためかれてこそのスカートめくり。
adjudicated.en: Indeed, a skirt flip needs to send in a flap.
comments: No, not planning to stop. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says skirt-flipping is worthwhile precisely because the target panics. The English leaves the person affected unstated and uses the malformed phrase 'send in a flap.'

highlights.text: a skirt flip needs to send in a flap

adjudicated.jp: やがて、ゆっくりとスカートが戻っていく。
adjudicated.en: Eventually, slowly, the skirt returns down.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...hah... haaah..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: とても嫌な汗をかいていた。
adjudicated.en: She broke into some really nasty sweat.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「パラシュート・デス・センテンスを成立させるための時間は、わずか０．０５秒に過ぎない。ではここで、そのプロセスをもう一度見てみることに―――」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "To bring a Parachute Death Sentence into existence, the time taken is a mere 0.05" and no more. Therefore, let us now see the process for ourselves one more t---"
comments: See CCA0006 and CCB2015 - that's 2x faster than Taichi's intercranial Ph*tosh*p and as fast as the summoning of the Harakiri Blade! Hmmm, 5+2 (the times he tries to go and do them) =7? OK, too forced. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese gives 0.05 seconds. The English replaces the unit with a stray closing quotation mark and adds 'and no more.'

adjudicated.jp: 霧ちんのスカートに手をかけた。
adjudicated.en: I had laid my hands on Kiri-chin's skirt and,
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese gives the immediate action of reaching for or taking hold of the skirt. Past perfect incorrectly moves it earlier, and the appended conjunction leaves the sentence unfinished.

highlights.text: I had laid my hands on Kiri-chin's skirt and,

adjudicated.jp: 「ちぇやーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "CH'EYAAAAAAAAAAA!!!"
comments: See CCB0006 (but not quite) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「久々に足技が出ましたぁぁぁぁ！」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "First time in so long we've seen her foot techniiiiique!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぎゃーーーーーーーーーーっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "G'hyaaaaaaaaaaa!!!"
comments: Hmmm, don't see it in either of these. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 踵落としが、途中で縦横無尽に軌道を変化させる。
adjudicated.en: The dropped heel instills endlessly changing trajectories left and right as they please.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says the descending heel changes its trajectory freely in every direction mid-kick. The English makes it instill multiple trajectories and assigns volition to those trajectories.

highlights.text: The dropped heel instills endlessly changing trajectories left and right as they please.

adjudicated.jp: まさに蹴りの乱気流だった。
adjudicated.en: It was definitely the turbulence of the kick.
comments: Same term as PDS -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 蹴りの乱気流 is a turbulence or flurry of kicks. The singular English phrase describes a property of one kick.

adjudicated.jp: 「おおおおおおお……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oooooooh..."
comments: PCP CCA0015B
おx7, still -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あなたは異常です！！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "You are abnormal!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 異常者扱いされた。
adjudicated.en: Treated as one abnormal.
adjudicated.assessment: 異常者 is a freak or abnormal person. The English uses the adjective 'abnormal' as an unheaded count noun.

adjudicated.jp: 「いてて……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "OwChCh..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「行こう、美希！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Let's go, Miki!"
comments: PCP CCA0015
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: プリプリ怒っている。
adjudicated.en: She's in a real huff of a mood.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……あーあ、行っちゃった」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...aaah, ah, she's gone."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩のチャレンジ精神は尊敬します」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Your spirit of self-challenge is admirable, Senpai."
adjudicated.assessment: チャレンジ精神 is a willingness or drive to take on challenges. 'Self-challenge' is a literalized, nonstandard compound.

adjudicated.jp: 「うむ。人間いつ死ぬかわからないしね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Indeed. Humans don't know the moment of their death."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「まぁ、君らものびのびと生きなさい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, you guys should live at ease and carefree too."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「うーす」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "'essir."
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese is a casual acknowledgment. The English adds a specifically subordinate, masculine 'yes, sir' relation.

adjudicated.jp: 「しかし……仲悪いですねぇ、お二人は」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Still... you get along bad, you two."
adjudicated.assessment: The standard English construction is 'you don't get along' or 'you get along badly'; the adjective cannot modify the verb.

adjudicated.jp: お互いに苦笑。
adjudicated.en: Reciprocal bitter smiles.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that they exchange wry smiles. The English is a verbless technical-sounding noun phrase, and 'bitter' overstates 苦笑.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺と霧とはミキミキを巡って恋のスキテキシュだからな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Because me and Kiri are Worthy Rivals of Love over you, Miki-Miki."
comments: 好敵手 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The subject pronoun must be 'Kiri and I,' the standalone 'because' leaves a fragment, and the common descriptive phrase is needlessly capitalized.

highlights.text: Because me and Kiri are Worthy Rivals of Love

adjudicated.jp: 「そうですね。すごく好敵手ですよね」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "That's right, yes. Really worthy rivals for sure."
comments: She's using Kiri as the Dragon. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: さらっと言われた。
adjudicated.en: She said that very casually.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「美希！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Miki!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ほーい。じゃせんぱい、またまたいつか」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Yeeeesh. Well, Senpai, someday someday see you again!"
comments: いつか、わたし -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese gives a cheerful acknowledgment and 'see you again sometime.' The English changes it to an exasperated 'yeesh,' duplicates 'someday,' and uses ungrammatical word order.

highlights.text: Yeeeesh. Well, Senpai, someday someday see you again!

adjudicated.jp: にぎにぎと挨拶を返す。
adjudicated.en: I return a merry greeting.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 美希は走って、霧に並んだ。
adjudicated.en: Miki ran over then lined up with Kiri.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

withheld.jp: 「だが、その長すぎる赤裸々タイムにより羞恥度は飛躍的に高まり、パラシュート効果の持続時間の終焉は、俺の命に対する死刑宣告をも意味するのである！　命と引き替えの大技、それがこのパラシュート・デス・センテンス！」
withheld.en: Taichi: "However, via this endlessly long Nuditeh time the degree of bashfulness swells by leaps and bounds, that when the perduration of the Parachute Effect enters its demise, it assuredly also signifies a Sentence of Death with regards to my life!"
comments: Sekirara, see CCB2007 again. Line was actually split exactly here in the console version -GHS
